label: KVP-3600, symptom 'hard_fault'
headline: Three of eight KVP-3600 inverters from a single 2024 week-32 build lot failed their IGBT power stage at three separate sites within 24 days, all OEM-authorised under warranty — pursue the remaining five units of that lot as a batch claim before coverage lapses.
action: Open a lot-level warranty case with Kelvara citing WO-2026-00626, WO-2026-00677 and WO-2026-00680, request the build records and IGBT/gate-driver lot traceability for the KVP36-2432C week-32 2024 block, and inspect or proactively schedule the five remaining units in that block while parts coverage is live.
reasoning: Decoding the asset_id (yyww block, confirmed by WO-2025-00543 where KVP36-1646D is described in-narrative as a 2016 build) shows a sharp step change rather than a model-wide effect: three distinct units from the 2024 week-32 build block (KVP36-2432C-0354, -0356, -0357) suffered IGBT power-stage failures at three different sites within 24 days (WO-2026-00626, WO-2026-00677, WO-2026-00680), each opened as a Kelvara warranty case and each authorised for a no-charge swap — exactly H1's predicted pattern of common build date plus common time-in-service, and inconsistent with H4's random-variation expectation of no block or calendar concentration. That block holds only 8 installed units (units_by_2024_manufacture_week, week 32), so three failures is not ordinary wear. H2 is partly right and is why confidence is not high: five members (WO-2024-00188, WO-2024-00195, WO-2025-00684, WO-2025-00695, WO-2025-00722) are self-clearing nuisance trips closed by RESET/NO-FAULT-FOUND with 1.8-3.3 h labour and no parts, and the controls show the same reset-and-hold behaviour on peer hardware (WO-2026-00034, WO-2025-00858, WO-2025-01192) — that slice is ordinary and should be stripped from the rate, but stripping it does not remove the 2432C IGBT trio. H3 is supported only as a data-quality defect, not as a rate explanation: parts_used is plainly wrong on several members (WO-2026-00677 and WO-2026-00680 read 'cooling fan' against narratives describing IGBT failures; WO-2025-00636 reads 'IGBT module' against a fan replacement), which corrupts parts analytics but does not manufacture three OEM-authorised IGBT claims out of one build week.
contradicting: The lot signal rests on three events from three units, and one of those units (KVP36-2432C-0354) had previously produced only a benign self-clearing trip (WO-2025-00722). Roughly a third of the cluster is nuisance-trip resets indistinguishable from the controls, so the headline 2.51x lift overstates the hardware problem. 2024-build units are about half the installed base and are still in warranty, which independently raises formal work-order generation (H3), so some of the 24xx concentration is reporting behaviour. Structured parts_used fields for this model are demonstrably unreliable, so any parts-based confirmation must come from the OEM case records, not the CMMS.

population_detail.description: KVP-3600 units from the 2024 week-32 manufacture block (asset prefix KVP36-2432C), of which three have already failed and five remain in service; adjacent 2024 Q3 weeks warrant a same-test check.
population_detail.basis: installed_base.units_by_2024_manufacture_week week 32 = 8 units; three distinct serials from that block (0354, 0356, 0357) produced OEM-authorised IGBT warranty claims within 24 days per WO-2026-00677, WO-2026-00680, WO-2026-00626.

hypotheses.statement: A discrete build lot of KVP-3600 units (serial block 'KVP36-2432C-xxxx' and neighbouring 24xx blocks) carries a defective IGBT/gate-driver power stage, and this lot alone accounts for the excess hard_fault rate over the peer median.
predictions: Cluster members concentrate disproportionately in a narrow asset_id serial range (24xxC, serials 0354-0379) relative to that range's share of the 376-unit cohort; KVP-3600 units outside that block should sit at or near the 0.018 peer-median rate.

Within the suspect block, failures should be dominated by parts_used containing 'IGBT module' or 'gate driver' and resolution codes PART-REPL / VENDOR-REFERRED / ESCALATED, not RESET or NO-FAULT-FOUND.

Failure dates within the block should cluster in time (e.g. the three 2026-06 warranty cases within 24 days at three different sites), consistent with a common commissioning date plus common time-in-service.
Repeat work orders on the same asset_id, or on sibling serials at the same site, should appear at above-baseline frequency after the first event.
Warranty wo_type should track the block, since a common build date implies a common warranty expiry.
discriminating_evidence: Cross-tabulate hard_fault count by serial block against installed count per block: a defect lot shows a step change at a block boundary; a model-wide problem or an artifact shows a flat distribution across blocks.

If units from the suspect block that were installed at low-temperature or low-irradiance sites fail at the same rate as those at hot sites, the cause is build-related rather than duty/environment-related.
OEM warranty case dispositions: multiple authorised no-charge IGBT swaps for one serial range is direct confirmation; scattered goodwill denials argues against.

hypotheses.statement: A large fraction of these events are self-clearing protective trips (firmware nuisance trips, e.g. fw 4.2.1) that are cleared by a manual reset with no component failure, so the 'hard_fault' count reflects trip sensitivity and truck-roll policy rather than hardware degradation.
predictions: A material share of cluster members carry resolution_code RESET or NO-FAULT-FOUND with parts_used empty or consumable-only (air filters), and labor_hours in the 1.8-3.3 h range, well below the 6.7 h cluster mean (113.6 h / 17 = 6.7).
Reported lost MWh per event should be low and concentrated in the part-replacement subset; the reset subset should contribute close to zero of the 8.7 MWh total.
Reset-type events should be over-represented on units still on older firmware, if firmware version is recorded or extractable from narratives.
Narratives should repeat the 'SCADA showed offline, drove out expecting comms, unit had stopped itself, restarted' pattern across multiple sites and techs.
If firmware campaigns were performed, hard_fault rate on upgraded units should drop after the upgrade date while the part-replacement rate stays flat.
discriminating_evidence: Split the 17 by resolution_code: if removing RESET / NO-FAULT-FOUND records drops the normalised rate to near the 0.018 peer median, the excess is trip sensitivity, not H1's hardware defect.
Check whether peer models' comparable nuisance trips are logged as a different symptom (e.g. 'offline' or 'comms') — if so the KVP-3600 excess is partly a labelling difference, pushing toward H3.
Recurrence flags: genuine hardware defects recur on the same asset; nuisance trips recur across many assets but rarely escalate to part replacement.

hypotheses.statement: The cluster is inflated by coding and extraction noise plus warranty-driven paperwork: 'hard_fault' is functioning as a catch-all symptom bucket for this model, and in-warranty units generate a formal work order for events that would be closed informally on out-of-warranty peers.
predictions: A high mismatch rate between parts_used and the extracted component within the cluster (e.g. 'cooling fan rplcd' with parts_used 'IGBT module'; 'dc contactor rplcd' with parts_used 'gate driver x4'; 'capacitor' component with parts_used 'gate driver'), indicating the structured fields are unreliable for this model.
Resolution_code should be internally inconsistent with the narrative in several records (e.g. PART-REPL with parts_used blank on WO-2025-00995; ADJUSTED on a fan replacement).
KVP-3600 should show correspondingly depressed counts in other symptom categories, so total CM work orders per unit for the model is close to peer median even though the hard_fault slice is 2.5x.
wo_type 'Warranty' should be over-represented in the cluster versus peer models' comparable events, and warranty events should cluster in units whose build year implies live coverage.
Terse near-identical one-line narratives ('hard fault; X rplcd; back online') should be concentrated among a small number of techs, indicating template entry rather than independent observation.
discriminating_evidence: Compare all-symptom CM work orders per unit for KVP-3600 versus peers: parity there with a hard_fault excess isolates the effect to symptom labelling, killing H1 and H2 as rate explanations.
Compare hard_fault rate for in-warranty versus out-of-warranty KVP-3600 units of similar age: if the excess disappears out of warranty, it is reporting behaviour, not hardware.
Re-extract symptom and component from raw narrative text independently and see whether the cluster survives; if the 17 fragment into several distinct symptoms, the cluster is an artifact.

hypotheses.statement: The lift is ordinary variation surfaced by multiple comparisons: 17 events against roughly 7 expected over a ~2.5-year window and 376 units is a small absolute excess that would be expected to appear in at least one model-symptom pair when many such pairs are scanned.
predictions: The number of model-symptom candidate pairs evaluated should be large enough that a 2.5x lift at n=17 is not extreme after multiplicity correction.
Splitting the 17 events by year should show no monotonic trend or acceleration; counts should be roughly Poisson-flat across 2024, 2025 and 2026 partial-year exposure.
Other symptoms for KVP-3600 should show lifts scattered both above and below 1.0 rather than uniformly elevated.
No single site, tech, serial block or calendar month should hold a disproportionate share of the 17 once exposure is normalised.
discriminating_evidence: Exact Poisson test on 17 observed versus expected-from-peer-rate exposure, then a multiplicity correction across all evaluated candidates; a corrected p that stays small refutes this hypothesis.
Hold-out test on a later time slice: if the KVP-3600 hard_fault rate reverts toward 0.018 in the next reporting period with no intervention, chance is the better explanation than H1.
Serial-block concentration test (same test as H1): strong concentration is inconsistent with random variation.
